news.title: Proof, if it were needed, why Traditionally bred Irish mares are so important to the export market.
news.body:
Proof, if it were needed, why Traditionally bred Irish mares are so important to the export market.
Looking at the eventing results for the week of 16.5 22 there were 49 classes in the UK and just 11 in the USA. Because not all classes have 10 finishers there were 480 T10Ps available in the UK and 99 in the USA. In the UK 38.1% were taken by Irish bred horses. A huge percentage when you remember that there are not only the homebred eventers but many Dutch and other continental imports competing at all levels. In the USA (with a very small number of classes) 23.2% were ISH. Considering the cost of shipping and the large number of ex racehorses used in the lower classes it is a credit to the Irish breeders that Ireland is the ‘go to’ stock for eventers in the USA.
Turning now at the horses who took a T10Place in the UK, 14.2% were themselves TIH of the 183 Irish bred horses (21.7% in the USA), 10.9% had TIH sires (4.3% in the USA) 12.5% had TIH Dam’s sires (26.1% in the USA) but most impressively 30% had TIH dams (30,4% in the USA). Because the vast majority of breeding mares in Ireland are plain ISH (either because they or in their parentage, there is lack of registered breeding or there are Warmblood genes within that pedigree) it is an impressive case of punching above their weight for those few TIH breeding mares left in Ireland.
If those responsible for the Irish Sport Horse (be they those that set out the future breeding plans or those that breed these valuable mares or the producers and sellers) don’t retain these TIH mares in Ireland, then the Traditional Irish Horse will become extinct.

Thank you Charlie Ripman as always for all the great statistics. We are very proud and determined to retain our traditional mares in our breeding programme. These high blood mares going back to old Irish blood lines are without doubt unique. We feel very strongly that they will present standout opportunities moving forward in a marketplace that will become so muddied by similarity.
Traditional Irish Horse Association #irishheritage #irishculture #irishhorse

news.title: I accept that this is early on in the research but I am looking at the horses that achieved a Top 10 Place in the UK in 2021 and were born in 2004 and later.
news.body:
I accept that this is early on in the research but I am looking at the horses that achieved a Top 10 Place in the UK in 2021 and were born in 2004 and later. There are 4,525 in total which includes all T10 Placed Irish bred horses.
Of the 376 with names beginning with A and B
77.7% had some TIH in their recent breeding or were themselves TIH.
22.9% were pure TIH.
5.8% had TIH Sires.
34.5% had TIH Dams.
10% had Dam’s Sires who were TIH.
This shows how influential TIH is in the breeding of Event horses aimed at export.

Irish Draught Horse Society Limited. Northern Ireland
January 20, 2022
Charlie Ripman continues to produce fantastic information highlighting the value of the Traditional Irish Horse (TIH) which as you will be aware can only have Irish Draught, Tb and / or Connemara blood in the pedigree.
